title: The 60-second node triage drill
jd: JD: proficiency with dmesg, journalctl, lspci, numactl, ethtool, iostat, perf, nvidia-smi, top/htop, ipmitool.
steps: For each resource (CPU, memory, disk, network, GPU) write the three USE questions: utilization, saturation, errors.
Run the first-minute set on any Linux VM: uptime, dmesg -T | tail, vmstat 1, mpstat -P ALL 1, pidstat 1, iostat -xz 1, free -m, sar -n DEV 1, ethtool -S <nic>. On a GPU box add nvidia-smi dmon.
Create one bottleneck at a time with stress-ng (CPU, memory), fio (disk) and iperf3 (network). Write down which tool exposes each one first.
Wrap the set into triage.sh that prints a one-page report with a verdict line per resource.
deliverable_html: triage.sh plus a table: symptom, command, how to read the output.
gem_html: Gregg's Linux Performance hub is the closest thing to an exam syllabus for the Linux-tools line in the JD.

title: Flame-graph a stalled GPU job
jd: JD: identify performance bottlenecks at node, accelerator and application layers.
steps: Run a small PyTorch training loop with a deliberately slow dataloader (num_workers=0). Watch SM utilization dip in nvidia-smi dmon.
Capture CPU stacks: perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 30, then perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl | flamegraph.pl > cpu.svg.
Load the same capture into FlameScope to see sub-second stalls that a flame graph averages away.
Fix the dataloader (workers, pin_memory, prefetch) and capture again. Show before and after side by side with GPU utilization.
deliverable_html: Before/after flame graphs with the GPU utilization chart and a three-line root cause.
question: GPU utilization is 40%. How do you decide whether the problem is CPU-side or GPU-side?

title: Trace a GPU container end to end

steps: Run a CUDA container with the NVIDIA runtime. Find the OCI spec the runtime received and list the /dev/nvidia* nodes inside the container.
Inspect the cgroup v2 device allow-list for that container and see which device majors are permitted.
Generate a CDI spec with nvidia-ctk cdi generate and run the same container through CDI. Compare the two paths.
Break it on purpose: remove one device from the allow-list, then mount mismatched driver libraries. Capture each error and the fix.
deliverable_html: A one-page sequence diagram: container start to GPU visible, with the two failure modes you reproduced.

Run cuda_memtest to look for memory faults the stress test can miss.
Define a pass rule, for example: no uncorrectable ECC, no sustained HW slowdown, temperature below your threshold, clocks within a band of the median GPU.
